name: Kavitark Ram Shriram
name_chinese: 卡维塔克·拉姆·斯里拉姆
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2006-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026); Hurun India (2015-2020); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: An early Google backer, Kavitark Ram Shriram has sold of most of his stock but remains on the board of its parent company, Alphabet.
Born in India, Shriram studied math at the University of Madras. After moving to the U.S. he joined Netscape in 1994 as an executive.
Later he became president of Junglee, an online comparison shopping firm acquired by Amazon in 1998. Ram took on a vice president position at Amazon.
He left Amazon and since 2000 has been investing in technology startups through his firm, Sherpalo Ventures.
His portfolio includes online invitation service Paperless Post, online HR service provider Gusto and mobile advertising company InMobi.
forbes_facts: In 2014, Shriram and his wife donated $61 million to engineering initiatives at Stanford University, which both of his daughters attended and where he is a trustee.
The name of Shriram's VC company, Sherpalo, comes from combining the words sherpa and Palo Alto.

name: Waleed Mohammad Al Zaabi
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Waleed Mohammad Al Zaabi is the founder and owner of Tiger Group, a United Arab Emirates-based real estate developer with offices in Dubai and Sharjah.
A civil engineer by training, Al Zaabi founded Tiger Group in 1976 as a construction firm and then moved into real estate development in 1996.
He later expanded into hospitality, manufacturing, agriculture and education in 2006. By 2014, Tiger Group had become a leading developer in Dubai and Sharjah.
Tiger Group has developed 50,000 apartments since 1976 and is building another 20,000 units, plus office and retail space, across the United Arab Emirates.
In 2024, Tiger Group launched Sky Tower, set to be the tallest residential tower in the world at 1,745 feet when it's completed in late 2029.

name: Eduardo Vivas
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2026); Hurun Global U40 (2026); Wikidata (2025); SEC insider holdings (2026)
forbes_bio: Eduardo Vivas is a pre-IPO investor in AI-powered advertising technology company AppLovin, which went public on the Nasdaq in 2021.
He owns 2% of AppLovin and has served on the company's board of directors since 2018.
Vivas is one of eight billionaires from AppLovin, including the company's cofounder and CEO Adam Foroughi.
Vivas tookover as COO of social shopping startup Humans, Inc. in 2024, when it acquired Curated, the online outdoor sports retailer Vivas cofounded in 2017. Humans shutdown in 2025.
Vivas previously served as head of product and talent solutions at LinkedIn from 2014 to 2017, after the company acquired Bright.com, which Vivas cofounded in 2011.

name: Brett Blundy
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2018-2025); Hurun Global (2020-2026)
forbes_bio: Brett Blundy is the founder of BBRC, a private investment company which has expanded from its retail roots into property, fund management, agriculture and technology.
He sold some property and retail interests in three IPOs. He's now building a beef cattle empire in northern Australia to feed Asian demand.
He has joined with cattle-station owners in Australia's Northern Territory to fund water supply, enabling properties to carry larger herds.
Fast fashion jewelry retailer Lovisa, which he cofounded in 2010 and boasts 900 stores worldwide, is embroiled in a lawsuit amid allegations of underpayment of staff dating back to 2019.
In 2021 Blundy sold key assets, including property fund Aventus, the listed Universal Store as well as the unlisted lingerie chain Honey Birdette to the Playboy Group.
forbes_facts: Blundy's interest in business started early. He grew up on a small farm near Melbourne where he and his four siblings would pick mushrooms to sell from a roadside stall for five cents a pound.
His career dream was to be a pilot, but that was thwarted when he failed the final year of school.
At age 20, Blundy bought a run-down record store in a suburb called Packenham with a friend. The business failed, and they had to take on day jobs to support it.

name: Nicolas Berggruen
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2009-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: The son of a wealthy art collector, Nicolas Berggruen was born in Paris and moved to the U.S. to attend New York University.
He first worked in real estate for Bass Brothers Enterprises before founding Berggruen Holdings in 1985 to manage his investments.
In 1988, he cofounded Alpha Investment Management, a fund of hedge funds operation that was sold to Safra Bank in 2004 for an undisclosed amount.
His Berggruen Holdings owns office buildings and apartments in Berlin, Germany and Portland, Oregon.
He is the founder and chairman of The Berggruen Institute, a think tank focused on developing ideas for the future of democracy and capitalism.
forbes_facts: A bachelor, Berggruen has settled down in Los Angeles with his 2 children, born in 2016 through an egg donor and 2 separate surrogates.

name: Mario Germano Giuliani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026)
forbes_bio: Mario Germano Giuliani is a healthcare investor who owns a minority stake in Royalty Pharma, the world's largest acquirer of pharmaceutical royalties.
Royalty Pharma went public in 2020 and has collected revenue slices of blockbuster drugs like Humira, Imbruvica, Lyrica and Xtandi.
Mario and his brother Giammaria also own stakes in Swiss investment company HBM Healthcare Investments and a number of biotech firms in the U.S.
The brothers share ownership of their family's pharmaceutical company, Giuliani, founded by their great-grandfather Germano in Milan, Italy in 1889.
They also own real estate investments in Europe and the U.S., including a planned commercial and residential project on a maritime platform in Monaco.
forbes_facts: The family company's best-known product is Amaro Giuliani, a herbal digestive remedy invented by Germano, a chemist, when he bought a pharmacy in Milan in 1889.

name: Sunil Vachani
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun India (2018-2019)
forbes_bio: Sunil Vachani is the founder and chairman of India-listed Dixon Technologies.
Vachani borrowed two million rupees ($27,600) from his father to set up the company in 1993 to manufacture TV sets.
The company makes products such as smartphones, washing machines and TVs for a range of clients including Samsung, Panasonic and Xiaomi.
The Noida-based company was listed in 2017.

name: Xiao Hongxing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun China (2024-2026); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Xiao Hongxing is the chairman of PCB manufacturing company Delton Technology, which went public  in Shenzhen in 2024.
The company completed its dual listing in Hong Kong in March 2026.
Xiao worked for Shengyi Electronics in Dongguan from 1988 to 1992 before starting his first business with his wife Liu Jinchan.

name: Kenneth Feld
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2014-2025); Hurun Global (2015-2026)
forbes_bio: Kenneth Feld owns live entertainment company Feld Entertainment, the parent company of Disney on Ice, Monster Jam and other shows.
Feld Entertainment grew out of Ringling Bros. circus, which was shut down in 2017 due to falling ticket sales.
His father, Irvin, bought Ringling Bros. circus in 1967 for $8 million.
Kenneth Feld took over in 1984 following his father's death.
Since then, he has worked to diversify beyond the Big Top. A Disney on Ice version of the hit movie Frozen has been particularly popular.
forbes_facts: While Feld remains CEO, he's preparing his three daughters to succeed him as ringmaster.
Feld has donated $1 million to Florida State University, which boasts one of the only two college circuses in the U.S.

name: Zhang Gongyun
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2021-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Zhang Gongyun is the former chairman and controlling shareholder of Shenzhen-listed Himile Mechanical Science and Technology (Shandong), a supplier of tire molds.
Himile's customers include Yokohama, Continental, Michelin and Bridgestone.
The company went public on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange in 2011.

name: Reagan Horton
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025)
forbes_bio: Reagan Horton's late father Donald Horton (d. 2024) founded homebuilder D.R. Horton in 1978.
He inherited a share of the family's more than 10% stake in the business, which is America's largest builder.
D.R. Horton has built more than 1 million homes across 126 markets in 36 states. It did $36.8 billion in fiscal 2024 sales.

name: Manuel Arango Arias
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026)
forbes_bio: Manuel Arango and his brothers, Jeronimo (d. 2020) and Placido (d. 2020) are credited for building one of Mexico's first major retailers and helping establish Walmart's presence in the country.
In 1958, as sales of their father's clothing factory dwindled, the trio founded the bargain retail chain Central de Ropa, later renamed Grupo Cifra.
The company owned the Bodega Aurrera stores, selling everything from groceries to home appliances.
The Arango's took the company public on the Mexican Stock Exchange in 1977. Fourteen years later, they embarked on a 50/50 partnership with Walmart to expand across Mexico.
In 1997, Walmart bought a majority stake in Grupo Cifra for $1.8 billion and took over Walmex (Walmart de Mexico).
forbes_facts: Arango won two Oscars in 1971 for producing "Sentinels of Silence," a documentary short about ancient Mexican civilizations.

name: Yao Kuizhang
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2001-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026); Hurun China (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Yao Kuizhang chairs Hebei Yangyuan Zhihui Beverage, a supplier of walnut drinks.
Yao owns 30% of the company.
Yao worked for Hebei Hengshui Laobaigan Liquor as a technician early in his career.

name: Frank Holding
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026)
forbes_bio: Frank Holding is Chairman and CEO of First Citizens Bank, a $23 billion (market cap) commercial banking chain, since 2008.
Holding's grandfather, Robert Powell Holding, became an employee of the bank in 1918, and became president by 1935, before passing it down to Frank's father, Lewis Holding.
Today, Frank and his four sisters collectively own about 20% of the bank.
Holding also serves as a board member of Wake Forest University.
